sections.heading: Opening
paragraphs: Per the file, at any given moment, (per the file) a cluster expects only one node to produce ledger entries. Per the file, by having only one (per the file) leader at a time, all nodes are able to replay (per the file) identical copies of the ledger. Per the file, the drawback of only (per the file) one leader at a (per the file) time, however, is that (per the file) a malicious leader is (per the file) capable of censoring votes and txs. Per the file, since censoring cannot be (per the file) distinguished from the network (per the file) dropping packets, the cluster (per the file) cannot simply elect a (per the file) single node to hold (per the file) the leader role indefinitely. Per the file, instead, the cluster minimizes (per the file) the influence of a (per the file) malicious leader by rotating (per the file) which node takes the lead.

Per the file, each node selects the expected leader (per the file) using the same algorithm, described below. Per the file, when the node receives a new signed ledger entry, it may be certain that an (per the file) entry was produced by the expected leader. Per the file, the order of slots (per the file) which each leader is (per the file) assigned a slot is (per the file) called a _leader schedule_. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Leader Schedule Rotation
paragraphs: Per the file, a node rejects blocks that are (per the file) not signed by the _slot leader_. Per the file, the list of identities (per the file) of all slot leaders (per the file) is called a _leader schedule_. Per the file, the leader schedule is (per the file) recomputed locally and periodically. Per the file, it assigns slot leaders (per the file) for a duration of (per the file) time called an _epoch_. Per the file, the schedule has to be computed far in (per the file) advance of the slots (per the file) it assigns, such that (per the file) the ledger state it (per the file) uses to compute the schedule is finalized. Per the file, that duration is called (per the file) the _leader schedule offset_. Per the file, solana sets the offset (per the file) to the duration of (per the file) slots until the next epoch.

Per the file, that is, the leader (per the file) schedule for an epoch (per the file) is calculated from the (per the file) ledger state at the (per the file) start of the previous epoch. Per the file, the offset of one (per the file) epoch is fairly arbitrary (per the file) and assumed to be (per the file) sufficiently long such that all nodes will have finalized their (per the file) ledger state before the (per the file) next schedule is generated. Per the file, a cluster may choose (per the file) to shorten the offset (per the file) to reduce the time (per the file) between stake changes and leader schedule updates. Per the file, while operating without partitions (per the file) lasting longer than an (per the file) epoch, the schedule only (per the file) needs to be generated (per the file) when the root fork (per the file) crosses the epoch boundary.

Per the file, since the schedule is (per the file) for the next epoch, (per the file) any new stakes committed (per the file) to the root fork (per the file) will not be active (per the file) until the next epoch. Per the file, the block used for (per the file) generating the leader schedule (per the file) is the first block (per the file) to cross the epoch boundary. Per the file, without a partition lasting (per the file) longer than an epoch, (per the file) the cluster will work as follows: A node continuously updates its own (per the file) root fork as it votes. Per the file, the node updates its leader schedule (per the file) each time the slot (per the file) height crosses an epoch boundary. Per the file, for example: Let's assume (per the file) an epoch duration of 100 (per the file) slots, which in reality is magnitudes higher.

Per the file, the root fork is (per the file) updated from fork computed (per the file) at slot height 99 (per the file) to a fork computed (per the file) at slot height 102. Per the file, forks with slots at (per the file) height 100, 101 were (per the file) skipped because of failures. Per the file, the new leader schedule (per the file) is computed using fork (per the file) at slot height 102. Per the file, it is active from (per the file) slot 200 until it is updated again. Per the file, no inconsistency can exist because every node that is voting with (per the file) the cluster has skipped (per the file) 100 and 101 when (per the file) its root passes 102. Per the file, all nodes, regardless of voting pattern, (per the file) would be committing to (per the file) a root that is (per the file) either 102, or a descendant of 102.

sections.heading: Leader Schedule Rotation with Epoch Sized Partitions.
paragraphs: Per the file, the duration of the (per the file) leader schedule offset has (per the file) a direct relationship to (per the file) the likelihood of a (per the file) cluster having an inconsistent (per the file) view of the correct leader schedule. Per the file, consider the following scenario: (per the file) Two partitions that are (per the file) generating half of the blocks each. Per the file, neither is coming to (per the file) a definitive supermajority fork. Per the file, both will cross epoch (per the file) 100 and 200 without (per the file) actually committing to a (per the file) root and therefore a (per the file) cluster-wide commitment to a (per the file) new leader schedule. Per the file, in this unstable scenario, (per the file) multiple valid leader schedules exist. Per the file, a leader schedule is (per the file) generated for every fork (per the file) whose direct parent is (per the file) in the previous epoch.

Per the file, the leader schedule is (per the file) valid after the start (per the file) of the next epoch (per the file) for descendant forks until it is updated. Per the file, each partition's schedule will (per the file) diverge after the partition lasts (per the file) more than an epoch. Per the file, for this reason, the epoch duration ought to be selected to be (per the file) much much larger then (per the file) slot time and the (per the file) expected length for a (per the file) fork to be committed to root. Per the file, after observing the cluster (per the file) for a sufficient amount (per the file) of time, the leader schedule offset may be selected based on (per the file) the median partition duration (per the file) and its standard deviation.

Per the file, for example, an offset (per the file) longer then the median (per the file) partition duration plus six (per the file) standard deviations would reduce (per the file) the likelihood of an (per the file) inconsistent ledger schedule in (per the file) the cluster to 1 in 1 million. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Leader Schedule Generation at Genesis
paragraphs: Per the file, the genesis config declares (per the file) the first leader for the first epoch. Per the file, this leader ends up (per the file) scheduled for the first (per the file) two epochs because the (per the file) leader schedule is also (per the file) generated at slot 0 (per the file) for the next epoch. Per the file, the length of the first two epochs may be specified in the (per the file) genesis config as well. Per the file, the minimum length of the first epochs has to be greater than or (per the file) equal to the maximum (per the file) rollback depth as defined in Tower BFT. sections.heading: Leader Schedule Generation Algorithm
paragraphs: Per the file, leader schedule is generated (per the file) using a predefined seed. Per the file, the process is as follows: Periodically use the PoH (per the file) tick height \(a monotonically (per the file) increasing counter\) to seed (per the file) a stable pseudo-random algorithm. Per the file, at that height, sample (per the file) the bank for all the staked accts with leader identities that (per the file) have voted within a (per the file) cluster-configured number of ticks. Per the file, the sample is called the _active set_. Per the file, sort the active set by stake weight. Per the file, use the random seed (per the file) to select nodes weighted (per the file) by stake to create (per the file) a stake-weighted ordering. Per the file, this ordering becomes valid (per the file) after a cluster-configured number of ticks. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Appending Entries
paragraphs: Per the file, the lifetime of a (per the file) leader schedule is called an _epoch_. Per the file, the epoch is split (per the file) into _slots_, where each (per the file) slot has a duration (per the file) of T PoH ticks. Per the file, a leader transmits entries during its slot. Per the file, after T ticks, all the nodes switch to the next scheduled leader. Per the file, validators must ignore entries (per the file) sent outside a leader's assigned slot. Per the file, all T ticks has to be observed by the (per the file) next leader for it (per the file) to build its own entries on. Per the file, if entries are not (per the file) observed \(leader is down\) (per the file) or entries are invalid (per the file) \(leader is buggy or (per the file) malicious\), the next leader (per the file) must produce ticks to (per the file) fill the previous leader's slot.

Per the file, if a leader incorrectly (per the file) builds on its own (per the file) ticks, the leader following (per the file) it must replace all its ticks.
